title: In the elect all sins are freely remitted through faith in Christ
source_text: IV. Quin docent in electis omnia peccata, quantumvis atrocia, gratis remitti atque condonari, nec ulla poena proprie & stricte sic dicta puniri. Idque quoniam, Deo per gratiam suam eos movente atque excitante, ante finem vitae serio convertuntur, atque peccato renunciant, & per fidem ad Christi meritum & justitiam confugiunt: ac propter eam a Deo peccatorum suorum remissionem consequuntur.
pass_a_gloss: Nay more, they teach that in the elect all sins, however atrocious, are freely remitted and pardoned, and are not punished with any penalty properly and strictly so called. And that because, God moving and stirring them by his grace, before the end of life they are seriously turned, and renounce sin, and by faith flee to Christ’s merit and righteousness: and on account of it they obtain from God the remission of their sins.
pass_b_english: For the elect, even atrocious sins are freely remitted—not repaid by strict penalty.
Grace turns them before death to flee by faith to Christ’s merit and righteousness.

choices.english: penalty properly and strictly so called
choices.why: Distinguishes paternal chastening from strict penal desert.
